automation_name: AI Security Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.rule: Only a source with a visible publication or update timestamp strictly inside this UTC interval qualifies. Date-only records were used only when their calendar date was unambiguously inside the interval; boundary-only, missing, ambiguous, and future dates were excluded.

source_method: Public-web collection using NVD's public CVE API as the primary vulnerability record, linked public researcher/vendor references, and federation-index checks. No private or local repository content was sent externally.
searched_topics: agent and tool security including MCP, plugins, browsers, delegated authority, and autonomous action
identity, authentication, authorization, credentials, and least privilege
model, dataset, dependency, artifact, runtime, cloud, hardware, and deployment supply chains
threat modeling, red teaming, security evaluation, assurance, monitoring, and release gates
AI security standards, regulation, governance, audit evidence, and risk management
public AI security incidents, mitigations, patches, disclosures, and lessons learned

qualifying_findings.title: Flowise public-chatflow endpoint exposes an MCP bearer token
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public CVE record with a VulnCheck CNA-source description and public Flowise source references; the product's public sunset page is linked as lifecycle context.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Flowise 3.1.3 through 3.1.4. An unauthenticated caller needs a public chatflow identifier; the affected chatflow uses its MCP-server configuration.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: A public agent entry point disclosed a delegated MCP authority token, allowing an unauthenticated actor to invoke tools and model-backed flow execution under the owner's quota and configured boundaries.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Flowise product background belongs in ai-wiki. Retain the MCP bearer-token disclosure, public-chatflow authorization boundary, lifecycle caveat, and credential-rotation implication in ai-security-wiki.

qualifying_findings.title: Flowise browser loaders permit DNS-rebinding SSRF to internal services
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public CVE record with a VulnCheck CNA-source description and linked public Flowise implementation references.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Flowise through 3.1.4. A low-privilege authenticated user who can configure a chatflow needs a DNS-rebinding domain and a Playwright or Puppeteer loader.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An agent-capable browser/document loader can turn user-controlled retrieval configuration into network authority over internal and cloud-metadata boundaries, with returned data entering the model context.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Flowise and browser-loader product background belongs in ai-wiki; general agent-development use of browser loaders belongs in ai-dev-wiki. Keep the SSRF, DNS-rebinding, metadata-boundary, and model-context exposure analysis locally.

qualifying_findings.title: AI Puffer stores unsanitized AI-generated comment replies as XSS
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public CVE record sourced from Wordfence, with linked WordPress plugin source and remediation changeset.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: AI Puffer / GPT AI Power WordPress plugin versions through 2.5.28. Exploitation requires an administrator-configured Comment Auto-Reply task set to Approve and approval of the attacker's comment.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is a model-output-to-browser trust-boundary failure: an automated AI reply can transform adversarial input into stored active content under a site workflow that appears to be a routine moderation automation.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: AI Puffer and WordPress-plugin catalog information belongs in ai-wiki. Retain the AI-output sanitization failure, approval precondition, stored-XSS boundary, and remediation reference locally.

qualifying_findings.title: agentic-radar loads an untrusted repository .env and can leak an OpenAI API key
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public CVE record sourced from VulnCheck, with linked public upstream remediation commit and v0.14.2 release.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: agentic-radar 0.7.0 before 0.14.2. Exposure requires scanning an attacker-controlled repository, an available OpenAI API key, and scan openai-agents or --harden-prompts calling OpenAI.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: A security scanner crossed the repository-trust boundary by accepting endpoint configuration from the artifact it analyzed, allowing prompt-hardening or agent scans to redirect credential-bearing model traffic.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: agentic-radar product background belongs in ai-wiki and general code-scanning workflow practice belongs in ai-dev-wiki. Keep the untrusted dotenv, endpoint redirection, credential-boundary, and v0.14.2 remediation implications locally.

upstream_routing_notes: Flowise catalog and product updates route to ai-wiki; this artifact keeps only the two security-specific MCP-token and browser-loader SSRF boundaries.
Browser-loader workflow adoption routes to ai-dev-wiki; DNS-rebinding prevention and internal-network containment remain ai-security-wiki concerns.
AI Puffer product background routes to ai-wiki; model-output sanitization and approval-automation attack implications remain local.
agentic-radar catalog information routes to ai-wiki and general scanner practice to ai-dev-wiki; repository-controlled configuration and credential egress remain local.

exclusions.reason: Excluded because no concrete vulnerability, exploit, mitigation, control, assurance result, regulatory change, or public incident was established.

confidence_notes: High confidence in the four CVE publication timestamps, affected descriptions, reference sets, and severity metadata because they were retrieved from NVD's public CVE API during this run.
The Flowise records are CNA-sourced through VulnCheck and identify no fixed version in NVD; the linked sunset page is lifecycle context, not proof that no downstream patch exists.
The AI Puffer record has a public WordPress remediation changeset, but the exact fixed plugin release should be confirmed before durable synthesis.
The agentic-radar remediation boundary is based on the linked upstream v0.14.2 release; verify installed distribution provenance and rotate keys if exposure is suspected.
follow_up_actions: At ingest, verify whether Flowise deployments use public chatflows, rotate MCP bearer tokens, restrict public endpoints, and establish whether a supported patched distribution exists.
At ingest, test Flowise URL-loader egress protections against DNS rebinding and cloud-metadata addresses; restrict browser-loader network reachability.
Confirm the AI Puffer fixed release corresponding to the WordPress changeset and review Comment Auto-Reply approval settings plus stored-reply sanitization.
Upgrade agentic-radar to v0.14.2 or later, ensure scanners do not load repository-controlled environment files, and rotate potentially exposed OpenAI API keys.
Route product-only background changes upstream; retain this publication-safe artifact as the portable provenance record after security-specific leaf synthesis and validation.
blockers: No collection blocker. Before durable synthesis, resolve Flowise supported-remediation status and exact fixed versions, verify the AI Puffer fixed release, and retain the CVE source-attribution qualifiers.

publication_safety.reason: The original collector artifact is retained locally outside version control because its credential-disclosure request sequence is not needed for the defensive wiki record.
publication_safety.preserved: Advisory identifiers, source URLs, affected versions and boundaries, attribution, security impact, routing, confidence, and mitigation follow-up are retained.
